records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents. From [the] depths I call to you, YHWH.

en.L: A song of ascents. From the depths I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: A song of ascents. From the deep waters I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am in deep trouble, and I am calling out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the depths: deep waters, deep distress
decisions.reason: The word (ma'amaqqim) is used of the deep waters of the sea (69:3, 15; Isaiah 51:10). Deep water is a picture of distress that threatens to drown a person; verses 3-4 show that here the distress includes the weight of guilt.

decisions.choice: I call: I have called and call now
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form usually used for past events, but it describes a cry that is still going on.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.
Readable gives the sense of the picture (m3).

source.text: אֲדֹנָי֮ שִׁמְעָ֪ה בְק֫וֹלִ֥י תִּהְיֶ֣ינָה אָ֭זְנֶיךָ קַשֻּׁב֑וֹת לְ֝ק֗וֹל תַּחֲנוּנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Lord, listen to my voice; may your ears be attentive to [the] sound of my pleas.

en.L: My Lord, listen to my voice; may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ears be attentive to the sound of my pleas for favor.
en.B: Lord, listen to me as I call! Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ears toward my cry for mercy.
en.R: Lord, hear me! Pay attention as I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for mercy.

decisions.reason: This is 'Adonai, "my Lord", a title, not the name. The psalm uses it three times (verses 2, 3, 6) alongside the name.
The word (tachanunim) comes from the verb "show favor" (123:2-3): the psalmist asks for what cannot be earned.

decisions.choice: your ears be attentive: pay attention
decisions.reason: The same request is made in Solomon's prayer (2 Chronicles 6:40; 7:15).
As elsewhere, 'Adonai in address is "my Lord" at Literal and "Lord" at Balanced and Readable.

records.literal_gloss: If iniquities you keep, Yah, Lord, who will stand?

en.L: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep iniquities, {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}, my Lord, who will stand?
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kept count of every wrong, Lord, who could stand before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kept a list of all our sins, who could ever stand before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in Exodus 15:2 and in "Hallelu-yah"). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: keep: keep watch on, keep a record of
decisions.reason: The verb (shamar) means to watch or keep. Here it is to keep watch over sins, storing them up against the sinner. The same verb is used of the watchmen in verse 6.

decisions.choice: who will stand: who could survive judgment
decisions.reason: To stand is to hold one's ground before a judge (1:5; 76:8). No one could if God counted every sin.
The word ('awon) means wrongdoing together with the guilt it brings.
Balanced and Readable say before whom no one could stand (m3).
As in verse 2.

records.literal_gloss: But with you [is] the forgiveness, so that you may be feared.

en.L: But with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [is] forgiveness, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} may be feared.
en.B: But forgiveness is found with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are held in awe.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgive, so that people will honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: The word (selichah) and its verb are used only of God forgiving (Nehemiah 9:17; Daniel 9:9).
Forgiveness does not make God less to be feared but more: those he forgives come to him in awe and worship him (1 Kings 8:39-40).
As in 33:18.

source.text: קִוִּ֣יתִי יְ֭הוָה קִוְּתָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י וְֽלִדְבָר֥וֹ הוֹחָֽלְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: I wait for YHWH, my soul waits, and for his word I hope.

en.L: I wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul waits, and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word I hope.
en.B: I am waiting for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; with all that I am I wait, and I hope in what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised.
en.R: With all that I am, I wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am hoping for what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised.

decisions.reason: The verb (qavah) is waiting that looks for something to come (27:14; 40:2).

decisions.choice: his word: what he has said, his promise
decisions.reason: The word (davar) here is what the LORD has spoken, the promise of forgiveness and rescue that the psalmist holds on to.

decisions.choice: my soul (L); with all that I am (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.
Balanced and Readable say what kind of word is meant (m2).

source.text: נַפְשִׁ֥י לַֽאדֹנָ֑י מִשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים לַ֝בֹּ֗קֶר שֹׁמְרִ֥ים לַבֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: My soul [is] for [the] Lord more than watchmen for the morning, watchmen for the morning.

en.L: My soul [waits] for my Lord more than watchmen for the morning, watchmen for the morning.
en.B: I long for the Lord more than night guards long for the morning, yes, more than night guards for the morning.
en.R: I want the Lord to come more than guards on night duty want the morning to come. Yes, more than they want the morning!

decisions.choice: watchmen for the morning: guards waiting for dawn
decisions.reason: Guards on the city walls or at the temple kept watch through the night and longed for dawn, when their watch ended and the dangers of the dark were past. The repetition makes the longing felt.

decisions.choice: my soul for the Lord: waits for the Lord
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb; "waits" is understood from verse 5.
As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.
'Adonai, "my Lord" (as in verse 2), here not in address.

source.text: יַחֵ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל־יְה֫וָה כִּֽי־עִם־יְהוָ֥ה הַחֶ֑סֶד וְהַרְבֵּ֖ה עִמּ֣וֹ פְדֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: Hope, Israel, to YHWH, for with YHWH [is] the loyal love, and much with him [is] redemption.

en.L: Hope, Israel, in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] loyal love, and abundant with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [is] redemption.
en.B: Israel, wait in hope for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! For loyal love is found with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} is redemption in full measure.
en.R: Israel, hope in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has faithful love for you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is more than ready to set you free.

decisions.reason: The psalmist's own hope (verses 5-6) becomes a call to the whole people to hope in the same way. The verb (yachal) is the one translated "hope" in verse 5.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps its commitments
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that is faithful to a bond and goes beyond what is owed: the LORD's commitment to his people, shown in kindness and rescue (Exodus 34:6-7).
As in Psalms 1-12: "loyal love" keeps both the love and the faithfulness of the word; Readable says "faithful love".

decisions.choice: redemption: setting free by a price or by power
decisions.reason: The word (pedut) is used of buying a slave's freedom and of the LORD freeing Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8). It is "much" with him: there is no limit to it.
Readable says what redemption is (m3).

records.literal_gloss: And he will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.
en.B: It is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who will redeem Israel from all its wrongs.
en.R: He is the one who will set Israel free from all its sins.

decisions.reason: The pronoun (hu') is written out for emphasis: it is the LORD and no other who will redeem.
Israel is to be set free not only from enemies but from its own guilt, the "iniquities" of verse 3. The angel's words in Matthew 1:21, "he will save his people from their sins", echo this line.
As in verse 7.
